title: Where the heat-sink surrogate fails: a quality-diversity map of its own error
description: A plate-fin heat sink described by three design numbers (fin count, fin height, approach air speed), an MLP surrogate fitted on a 2000-case ducted-forced-convection campaign (0.8-3.0 m/s), and a MAP-Elites archive over a behaviour space that is not the design space: thermal resistance against mass, both from the closed-form reference. The fitness is the surrogate's own relative error, so the archive returns where the model is wrong as cells with a number, a design and a behaviour condition, with the cases the reference cannot answer refused rather than archived. The same archive with sense=min is the design map: the least fan power that achieves each (Rth, mass) cell. The failure search is compared with random and Latin-hypercube sampling at the same 600-evaluation budget over 5 seeds.

metrics.name: qd_max_error
metrics.how: largest stored Rth relative error found by the quality-diversity search, mean over 5 seeds at 600 evaluations each (62.4%-72.3% over the seeds)

metrics.name: random_max_error
metrics.how: the same number for uniform random sampling at the same 600 evaluations, mean over 5 seeds (54.0%-62.0%)

metrics.name: latin_max_error
metrics.how: the same number for Latin-hypercube sampling at the same 600 evaluations, mean over 5 seeds (55.7%-71.4%)

metrics.name: qd_minus_random_max_error
metrics.how: paired by seed, qd - random: +4.3, +4.7, +13.7, +8.5, +12.5 points, positive on all five seeds

metrics.name: qd_minus_latin_max_error
metrics.how: paired by seed, qd - latin: -8.0, +11.0, +16.5, -0.4, +0.1 points: the mean favours qd and three of five seeds do, so the two are within seed noise

metrics.name: qd_failing_cells
metrics.how: cells whose elite error is above the 10% tolerance, mean over 5 seeds (random 43.0, latin 40.8)

metrics.name: qd_fill
metrics.how: occupied cells over the 10x10 grid, mean over 5 seeds (random 0.578, latin 0.558)

metrics.name: design_map_cells
metrics.how: cells filled by the design map (sense=min, fitness = fan power), seed 0, 600 evaluations; the map is the committed figure

metrics.name: known_near_pass_error
metrics.how: the archive's own elite error for the 0.6 m/s near-pass case (14 fins, 30 mm, below the campaign's 0.8 m/s floor), which the search was not told about

checks.name: qd_beats_random_at_equal_budget
checks.detail: paired by seed over 5 seeds: +4.3 to +13.7 points, positive on every seed
checks.label: the failure search finds a larger verified error than random sampling at 600 evaluations

checks.name: qd_beats_latin_at_equal_budget
checks.detail: mean +3.8 points, but seeds 0, 3 and 4 are -8.0, -0.4 and +0.1: no per-seed advantage over Latin hypercube
checks.label: the failure search beats Latin-hypercube sampling on every seed (it does not; only the mean favours it)

checks.name: inapplicable_cases_refused
checks.detail: the 0 m/s fan-off case is refused by the reference (natural convection, junction above its limit) instead of being archived at a meaningless error; 161 of 600 cases refused per run
checks.label: cases the reference physics cannot answer are refused, not reported as model failures

checks.name: known_failure_recovered
checks.detail: the 0.6 m/s near-pass case comes out at 10.5%, in the failing set, without being told about it
checks.label: a failure already known from the campaign envelope is found by the search

references: Mouret & Clune, Illuminating search spaces by mapping elites, arXiv:1504.04909 (2015)

Bar-Cohen & Rohsenow, Thermally optimum spacing of vertical, natural convection cooled, parallel plates, J. Heat Transfer 106 (1984)
